one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results are not expected inside the window: Q2 was reported Aug 6 and CEG historically reports Q3 in the first week or so of November, so earnings most likely land just after 2026-10-29 (unconfirmed date). In-window industry events: PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement was slated to open around Sept 30 with bids through November (no clearing result expected in October); FERC/PJM follow-through on co-location and large-load rules; pre-positioning ahead of the December 2029/30 BRA, which is already collared at a $325/MW-day cap. None is a binary price event for CEG. Offsetting drifts: the stock just fell 13% (Sep 9-18) on the Calpine-holder share overhang and rising yields and bounced ~4% to $264.58, so mild short-term reversal plus a steady buyback bid argue slightly up, while the remaining ~5.9% holder stake (post June secondary) can keep coming to market. Net: near-symmetric lognormal centred ~$266 (tiny upward tilt) at ~13% monthly sigma (47%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (2028E EPS ~$14.3 x 20x = $286, 70%) and a haircut consensus analyst target ($347 x 0.80 = $278, 30%) gives ~$284 12 months out.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus compilations show $13.34 (20 analysts) and $12.75; I use ~$13.0, roughly the midpoint, reflecting ERCOT softness and capped PJM capacity.

2027E $13.0 grown ~10%, the low end of management's rolling >10% base growth target; supported by capacity cleared at $325-333/MW-day through May 2029, Crane restart in 2027 and ongoing buybacks ($2.8B authorization left) lowering share count.

CEG trades ~22x 2026 guidance midpoint and ~20x 2027E today at $264.58; peers VST and TLN are also down >20% YTD, so the sector de-rating looks structural (ERCOT softness, PJM collar, AI-demand doubts). I hold today's ~20x rather than assume a re-rating back to the 30x+ of 2025.
The mean target fell from $405 (Dec 2025) to ~$349 while the stock fell faster; targets have lagged sector de-rating, so I discount them ~20%.

bear.story: AI power demand narrative weakens further (hyperscaler capex digestion, data-center load forecasts cut), political pressure keeps PJM capacity collared or tightened after 2029/30, backstop procurement and 'connect and manage' add supply expectations, ERCOT stays soft, and the remaining Calpine-holder stake keeps overhanging. EPS ~$12.7 on 15x.

base.story: Earnings grow ~8-10% on capped-but-high PJM capacity revenue ($325-333/MW-day), Crane restart in 2027, a few more nuclear PPAs (pipeline 'robust and active'), and buybacks; multiple stays ~20x as overhang clears.

bull.story: One or more large hyperscaler/co-location nuclear deals at premium prices (co-location rules finalized in IPPs' favour), PJM scarcity (6.8 GW shortfall, uncapped $555/MW-day) translates into higher forward energy and contract prices, and the multiple re-rates to ~26x on 2028E ~$14.5.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$195 (about 15x 2027E EPS and well under the 52-week low of $228.63), the stock would be pricing a lasting cut to earnings rather than overhang/yield noise: e.g. a regulatory change that caps or claws back PJM capacity or energy revenue beyond the current collar, loss/restructuring of a flagship nuclear PPA, a major nuclear operating problem, or a sharp downward reset of data-center load in PJM forecasts.

catalysts.event: PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement bid window (targets ~6.8 GW shortfall / up to ~15 GW new supply by 2031)
Q3 2026 results; possible 2027 commentary and new PPA announcements
PJM 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction (collar extended, cap ~$325/MW-day)

Further sales by remaining Calpine-legacy holders (ECP, CPPIB, TRS; ~5.9% stake after June secondary)
Price-collar debate for auctions beyond 2029/30; state/federal affordability interventions

key_uncertainties: Whether data-center load materializes as fast as PJM forecasts or hyperscalers slow capex
Political/regulatory ceiling on PJM capacity prices beyond the 2029/30 auction
Pace and pricing of new nuclear PPAs (only ~30% of baseload contracted; peer Talen has signed nothing new beyond AWS)
ERCOT and gas-price driven energy margins from the Calpine fleet
Remaining share overhang from Calpine consideration holders and interest-rate sensitivity of the multiple
reasoning: Industry lane. The value chain tells a split story. Supply is tight: PJM's 2028/29 BRA cleared at the $325/MW-day cap for the third straight auction, $555 uncapped ($777 in ComEd), with a 6.8 GW reserve shortfall and only ~525 MW of new supply; CEG cleared ~18.9 GW (~$2.2B). PJM West forwards are ~$84-85/MWh for 2027-28 on-peak with gas under $3, and PJM is running a backstop procurement. So CEG's 2027-28 capacity revenue is locked in and energy prices are firm. But the upside is being capped by politics (collar extended to 2029/30, White House and governors' principles putting new-capacity cost on data centers), ERCOT is soft (hit CEG's Q2 and VST), and peers all de-rated: VST, TLN and NRG are each down >20% YTD even as they report record EBITDA and raise guidance. Talen has not signed PPAs beyond AWS, so contracting is slow even though the hyperscaler capex backdrop (~$600-700B in 2026) is intact. The FERC co-location order is a medium-term positive. The company-specific drag is technical: Calpine-holder stock (June $3.1B secondary; 5.9% still held) plus rising yields. That is offset by buybacks ($2.2B YTD, $2.8B left) and a beat-and-raise (2026 guide $11.50-12.50). Valuation: ~20x on 2028E $14.3 gives ~$286, blended with haircut targets to ~$284, about 7% above spot. Scenarios $190/$285/$380 at 25/50/25 give a mean of ~$285. For the ladder I used a lognormal with median ~$275 and sigma 0.40, a bit below the 47% realized vol because part of that came from a one-off overhang, with slightly fattened far tails. Research was limited to ~20 web queries/fetches; I did not check prediction markets or X, and did not look at options.
